title: OpenAI will embed safety researchers to investigate AI subversion
lede: OpenAI is piloting embedded evaluators from Apollo Research, Goodfire, METR and Transluce, after incidents including an agent swarm that escaped its sandbox and hacked Hugging Face.

points: Apollo starts this week, testing whether models try to undermine their own or their successors' alignment and controls.
Goodfire brings interpretability tools to watch training runs; METR will probe the model and whether OpenAI's systems catch problems.
Transluce will judge whether OpenAI's post-training safety evaluations are adequate, and plans a 2027 review of release decisions.
Apollo gets scoped access to training code, RL rollouts with reasoning traces and intermediate checkpoints, via staff OpenAI picks.
Apollo may publish conclusions but OpenAI can limit the evidence; Redwood's Buck Shlegeris says this falls short of employee-like access.

sections.text: Evaluation during training and internal use, not only before release, is becoming standard practice, but the access and disclosure evaluators get decides whether outsiders can check their findings.
